name: update-notion-when-rescheduled-in-buttondown

replaces.state: disabled 2026-08-07, trigger claim released, zero runs
replaces.why: The Durables UI migration tool created that container with is_private: true, violating repo rule 7, and visibility cannot be changed after creation — `update-workflow` takes only --name/--description and no publish command exposes a visibility flag. Recreating was the only fix, and cheap here because the trigger is a poll: no external catch URL to rewire and nothing to reconfigure on the Buttondown side. Safe to delete once this container has caught a real reschedule.

trigger.notes: Polling trigger on the private `Buttondown Unofficial #2` app (source: ~/Repos/zapier-buttondown). Polls GET /v1/emails?status=scheduled&ordering=-creation_date&page=1, keeps rows with a publish_date, and dedupes on `${id}:${publish_date}` so each reschedule is a fresh event. Emits email_id, publish_date, subject, body, status, creation_date, description, slug. Durable triggers cannot set a polling interval, so this runs at the account default — any interval the classic Zap had was silently dropped at migration.

connection_notes.notioncliapi_connection: Legacy numeric id carried over from the migrated version; it is the work.flowers Notion connection (UUID 02b73654-15c8-85c3-b16a-07304d2beb17), the same one `new-buttondown-subscriber-update-in-notion` uses. Confirmed by the pinned NotionCLIAPI 2.39.1 (the Knoxx connection is on 2.32.0) and by Newsletter Issues resolving from it. Never the `Knoxx | Dennis #2` connection (02b95b31-c152-8800-9036-1107e08f70da). `run-durable` wants the nested UUID form `{"notioncliapi_connection":{"connectionId":"02b73654-…"}}`; publish takes this numeric form.
connection_notes.TableCLIAPI: search/find_record against Zapier Table 01KNJN2MSBAJVXRME6M1Y65F5B — Zapier Tables need no connection and cost no tasks.

notion.property_written: Send Date (date) via `properties|||Send Date|||date__start`, which requires use_zapier_datetime_fields: true alongside it
notion.template_mode: N/A — this updates an existing page and never creates one, so repo rule 5 does not apply

zapier_table.name: Email Newsletter ID Mapping

fields.f1: Page ID (Notion Newsletter Issues page id)

zapier_table.result_shape: find_record wraps each hit as {new, old, record_id, table_id} — values at data[0].old.data.<fieldId> — and returns {data: []} on a miss.

fixes_applied_vs_migrated_version: Empty-lookup guard. The migrated code read `data[0].old.data.f1` unguarded, so an email with no mapping row threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'old')` and burned all 5 step retries (reproduced: run 019fdb87-d810-7abb-9e91-d95c4b2b1c4d). Since the trigger polls EVERY scheduled Buttondown email, not just ones sent from Notion, a miss is a routine non-event — it now logs and returns `{skipped: "no-notion-page-for-email"}`.
Added the repo rule 2 source-of-truth header comment.
Tightened the cast to a `TableHit` type, so the file typechecks under --strict (the migrated version failed TS2571 on line 46).

InputSchema is now actually used: a payload missing email_id/publish_date throws naming the keys received, instead of writing `undefined` into Notion. Verified it tolerates the trigger's full nine-field payload (zod strips unknown keys).
known_limitations: Unscheduling is invisible. Moving an email back to draft removes it from the status=scheduled list, which produces no event, so the Notion Send Date is never cleared. Only sets and changes propagate.

use_zapier_datetime_fields passes the Buttondown UTC string through rather than converting to the account timezone, so Send Date is rewritten from Notion's +08:00 form to the equivalent +00:00 form. Same instant, renders identically in Notion, and the outbound Zap reads date.start where both forms are unambiguous.
description: Buttondown send date set or changed -> write it back onto the Notion Newsletter Issues page, resolved via the Email Newsletter ID Mapping Zapier Table. Reverse leg of notion-newsletter-to-buttondown.
